placements.role: Operates nuclear and gas generation fleets that contract firm electricity to data-center customers.

role_evidence.claim: Constellation's full-year 2025 results describe its nuclear fleet and Calpine gas fleet as supplying power and grid connectivity for data centers.

business_summary: Constellation Energy Corporation is a Nasdaq-listed competitive power producer and retail energy supplier, separated from Exelon in 2022. It operates the largest nuclear fleet in the United States and, following the Calpine acquisition, a large gas fleet alongside it. Its commercial proposition to hyperscale buyers is long-dated, carbon-free firm power contracted directly from that fleet.

exposure_summary.narrative: Constellation has one placement, on energy-generation, which is position one of the chain and the raw input every downstream link depends on. The link is scored EMERGING rather than UNDISCOVERED and is not the money corner, which matters: this is the part of the chain that has already been narrated as an AI trade. The mapped role evidence rests on the full-year 2025 results release. The fetched second-quarter 2026 earnings deck does not contain the phrase data center at all; it describes long-term nuclear power purchase agreements and regulatory progress for large load customers instead, which is the same economics in the company's own vocabulary but is not a data-centre attribution.

disclosed_revenue_exposure.basis: No data-centre revenue percentage is disclosed. The fetched second-quarter 2026 deck (accession 0001868275-26-000097) discloses megawatts of long-term nuclear contracts and a contracted share of baseload clean generation by 2032, but no revenue share attributable to data centres.

implied_fcf_cagr.basis: Free-cash-flow CAGR the current enterprise value 104760000000.0 implies over a 5-year explicit period on base FCF 1288000000.0, solved by bisection on FCF CAGR at a 0.09 discount rate and 0.025 terminal growth. The discount rate and terminal growth are assumed, so the solve is an assumption-dependent expectation reading, not a reported figure.

horizon_spread.basis: Spread between the implied CAGR solved over the shortest and longest explicit periods in quality.reverse_dcf.implied_by_horizon ({'5': 0.4611, '7': 0.3327, '10': 0.244}). It measures how much of the expectation reading is a horizon convention rather than a statement about price, and inherits the same assumed discount rate and terminal growth.

crowdedness_caveats: The energy-generation link carries a crowdedness score of 50 and its rationale says merchant power names were discovered in the 2024 to 2026 waves and re-rated hard. Constellation is one of the names that rating describes.
data/market/CEG.json pcs records 20 analysts and 83.1% institutional ownership as of 2026-08-29, axis-B SATURATED, with axis-A DARK at 88.2 under an ADVISORY gate.

The reverse DCF in data/market/CEG.json implies the highest FCF growth rate in this batch over a five-year explicit period, on the widest horizon spread. A high implied rate on a wide spread is where a crowded expectation and a horizon convention are hardest to tell apart.

data_gaps: Piotroski is PENDING_DATA in data/market/CEG.json quality on the missing cost_of_revenue_fy input; Beneish is PENDING_DATA on missing cost_of_revenue_fy and sga_fy. Companyfacts coverage for this issuer is missing gross profit, cost of revenue and SG&A.
No data-centre revenue share is disclosed, and the fetched second-quarter 2026 deck does not name data centres at all.
The fetched EDGAR document is an earnings-call presentation exhibit, which is a slide deck: numbers in it are often non-GAAP and reconciled only in an appendix.
Adjusted operating earnings, the company's own headline measure, is non-GAAP and is not a canonical profile metric; only GAAP companyfacts figures are used above.

disposition.basis: Complete medium profile on position one of the chain, backed by a filing-dated role. Retained rather than advanced because the link is EMERGING rather than the money corner, the name has already re-rated, the balance sheet is the only leveraged one here, and the expectations reading is both the most demanding and the least stable across horizons in this batch.

confidence_audit.basis: Counts cover the canonical metric fields only. VERIFIED is a figure read directly off SEC companyfacts as reported. INFERRED is a figure computed from SEC companyfacts, with the derivation named in its basis; where a market price enters the computation the basis says so explicitly, because the price leg is the repo's own dual-source market plane (data/market/CEG.json, price_status AGREED) and not an issuer document. SPECULATIVE is reserved for the reverse-DCF solve, whose discount rate and terminal growth are assumed. NULL is a field looked for and not found, never estimated.
